Alabama.focus: Eleven statewide initiatives: IT hubs, telehealth, maternal and cancer regionalization, workforce
Alabama.description: Alabama plans to modernize and integrate its rural health system through eleven statewide initiatives, from regional IT and cybersecurity hubs to maternal, cancer, behavioral health and EMS programs.
initiatives: Regional IT hubs supporting EHR integration, IT infrastructure and security.
Digital obstetric regionalization and telerobotic ultrasound.
Converting community mental health centers into Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics.

Alaska.focus: Six community-led initiatives from maternal health to technology
Alaska.description: Alaska plans to strengthen community-led, regionally designed health systems that provide a full continuum of care as close to home as possible, through six flexible, voluntary initiatives.
initiatives: Strengthening maternal and child health as a foundation for healthy families.
Expanding primary, behavioral, oral, specialty, emergency, home- and community-based and post-acute services.
Voluntary payment models that shift rural providers from volume-based reimbursement toward financial sustainability.
Consumer digital devices, telehealth, appropriate AI, cybersecurity, interoperability and testing new delivery modalities.

Arizona.focus: Workforce, priority health grants, access and resilience
Arizona.description: Arizona's plan, led by AHCCCS, targets behavioral health, chronic disease, maternal and child health and the rural workforce through four strategic pillars.
initiatives: Recruiting, training and retaining providers through rural clinical rotations, residency programs and career and technical education.
Behavioral health and SUD treatment, chronic disease prevention, and maternal, fetal and infant health.
Telehealth infrastructure plus mobile and satellite care delivery.
Shared-service networks, subsidized EHR licenses and back-office capacity to cut fixed costs.

Arkansas.focus: HEART, PACT, RISE AR and THRIVE
Arkansas.description: Arkansas plans a statewide program built on four initiatives covering prevention, care coordination, workforce and telehealth.
initiatives: Prevention and chronic disease programs, school and community wellness, nutrition and physical activity.
Integrated networks, expanded primary and specialty access, scope-of-practice changes and facility investments.
Residency, preceptorship and leadership training plus recruitment and retention incentives.
Telehealth platforms, remote monitoring for chronic disease, EMS modernization and virtual care.
